anzsic_codes.name: Automotive Body, Paint and Interior Repair

merger_description:
Australian Motor Group Pty Ltd (**AMG**) (via a specialised vehicle, AMG Headquarters Eighteen Pty Ltd (**AMGHQ18**)) proposes to acquire substantially all the assets of the motor vehicle dealership business trading as Mudgee Toyota, which is owned by Dawnaco Pty Ltd. Mudgee Toyota operates from leased premises at 30 Burrundulla Avenue, Mudgee NSW 2850.

AMG, AMGHQ18 and its connected entities are majority owned by Mark James Fitzgerald who owns, controls and operates a group of 12 franchised automotive dealerships across 32 locations in New South Wales: Sydney (which covers Windsor, Castle Hill, Hornsby, Pennant Hills, Chatswood, Brookvale and Mona Vale), Newcastle and Taree (together, the **AMG Dealerships**).

The AMG Dealerships currently represent 17 vehicle brands as an authorised dealer of new vehicles, including Toyota, BMW, Mazda, Ford, Hyundai, Kia, Subaru, Volkswagen, Nissan, Volvo, GMSV, Jeep, Alfa Romeo, Fiat Pro and Suzuki. The AMG Dealerships also sell a range of used vehicles, in addition to providing vehicle servicing and repairs, genuine manufacturers’ spare parts and accessory sales, as well as facilitating finance, insurance and customer care products in connection with the vehicle transactions.

Mudgee Toyota is a new and used car retailing business that operates a franchised automotive dealership in the Mudgee area (located in central west NSW). Mudgee Toyota represents one vehicle brand as an authorised dealer, being Toyota. Mudgee Toyota also supplies manufacturers’ spare parts and accessories, aftermarket servicing and repairs and finance and insurance solutions.

While AMG and Mudgee Toyota both supply new Toyota vehicles and used cars, spare parts, aftermarket vehicle servicing and financing and insurance solutions, AMG does not presently operate any authorised car dealerships in the Mudgee area and is not an authorised dealer for Toyota in this area.

The transaction will occur by way of a business sale and purchase agreement.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver and had regard
to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is a small overlap between AMG and Mudgee Toyota in
the supply of new and used cars in the Mudgee region
b. there are alternative suppliers of new and used cars in the
Mudgee region and alternative Toyota dealerships in the
wider region.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
